newsitem.title: USA: Intermountain Power seeks sale to Calif. customers.
newsitem.headline: Intermountain Power seeks sale to Calif. customers.

text.p: Intermountain Power Agency (IPA), based in Utah, is negotiating the sale of its coal-fired power generating operations to six California cities, including Los Angeles, a company official said Wednesday.
"We are exploring the formation of a new joint action agency to buy Intermountain Power," said Reed Searle, general manager of the Utah power agency.
IPA owns a 1,640 megawatt coal-fired power station in Delta, Utah.
The six California cities are obligated to purchase around 95 percent of the plant's output, with 26 Utah cities purchasing the remainder, Searle said.

IPA has been plagued by high costs related to its heavy debt load and above-market coal price contracts. Late last year, Standard and Poor's rating agency lowered its rating on IPA's $4.613 billion power supply revenue bonds.
Searle said the talks are aimed at aligning the financial obligations of the California customers with management responsibilities.
The new ownership arrangement would also be expected to generate cost savings. Also, the purchaser group would pay IPA sufficient funds to fully discharge all of the agency's oustanding bonds.
"The California utilities have the majority of financial obligations but management is still a landlord-type arrangement," Searle added.
In addition to the Los Angeles Department of Water and Power, municipal utilities for the cities of Anaheim, Riverside, Pasadena, Glendale and Burbank are involved in the talks, IPA said.
The agency hopes to have a memorandum of understanding for the sale by July, with the actual transaction expected to take 10 months to complete.
"There are dozens of contracts to be signed and dozens to be terminated," Searle said.
